You own `services/analytics` (`brh_analytics`): the scope that turns the BRH
corpus into stats, charts and postable images. Work there. Step outside it only
when a change genuinely requires it, and say so when you do.

## Read first, every time

1. `services/analytics/DESIGN.md` — the style guide. It is binding, not
   decorative.
2. `services/analytics/README.md` — the structure and the live families.
3. `services/analytics/src/brh_analytics/palette.py` — the tokens.
4. `PROGRESSION.md`.

## The shape you are extending

A **family** is a package under `src/brh_analytics/` that owns a source and its
copy. `inventory` is the live one: `ledger.py` reads `corpus.crawl_urls`,
`findings.py` writes the copy.

Above the families sits a shared, **domain-free** layer — `palette.py`,
`formatting.py`, `assets.py`, `charts.py`, `finding.py`, `posts.py`,
`families.py`. It must never learn about a domain type: that is what lets the
next family inherit the whole design system for free.

Adding a family is a package exposing `build() -> tuple[Finding, ...]` (and
optionally `tables()` for the dashboard), plus one line in `families.py`.
Nothing else changes — the CLI and the dashboard iterate the registry.

Output mirrors the code: `out/<family>/<finding-slug>-<canvas>.png`.

## Hard rules

- **`palette.py` is the only place a hex value is written.** A new colour means
  a new token there, used by name, plus its row in `DESIGN.md` — including its
  contrast ratio, which `palette.check()` computes. Never invent a colour in a
  chart or a post.
- **`DESIGN.md` is the contract.** Breaking a rule in it (a new chart type, a
  canvas, a colour role) is allowed — but change `DESIGN.md` in the same commit
  and say why. A rule that lives only in the code is a rule that will be broken.
- **Charts are naked.** No title, no legend chrome, no source line: the post
  owns those. `charts.py` takes numbers and labels, never a domain type.
- **A bucket is never charted.** "Autres", "Divers", "N/A" outrank real
  categories and contradict the headline. Their size belongs in the caption.
- **Do not chart the healthy majority when the story is the exception.**
- **Every figure in the copy is derived from the data**, never typed in. A
  number that can drift from its source eventually will.
- **French only, with French typography.** Use `fr_number`, `fr_date`,
  `fr_bytes` from `formatting.py`: narrow no-break spaces inside numbers,
  no-break space before `%`, `15/10/2026` dates. The corpus is French-only
  (ADR-0004) — no translation, no English chrome.
- **The inventory family reads the crawl ledger, not the corpus.** That is ops
  data, so ADR-0006 does not apply to it. A family that reads *the corpus* must
  go through `RetrievalService` — never Postgres or Pinecone directly.

## The copy

The headline makes a claim, the figure proves it, the caption says where the
number came from. One idea per asset.

Specific beats clever: "347 documents publiés en deux jours" earns its click;
"un pic surprenant" does not. No exclamation marks, no "données fascinantes",
no superlative the data cannot carry.

Honesty is the house style. When the taxonomy is fuzzy or the data incomplete,
say so in the caption — the `familles` post admits a third of titles resist
classification, and the `qualite` post is *about* upstream damage. That candour
is the product, not a hedge.

## Verify before claiming anything works

```bash
uv run python -m brh_analytics                            # every family, square
uv run python -m brh_analytics --family <slug> --size portrait
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
uv run pytest -q
uv run python -c "from brh_analytics import app"           # dashboard smoke
```

Then **open the PNG you produced** at `out/<family>/<slug>-square.png`. Render
every canvas you touched: the layout is written on a 1080 grid and divided by
`scale`, so a change that looks right in a square post can still break a
landscape card. A chart you have not looked at is a chart you have not checked.

## Gotchas that cost time

- `out/` is generated and gitignored. Never hand-edit it, never commit it.
- Montserrat and Inter are **not bundled**, so everything currently renders in
  DejaVu. Fonts load from `assets/fonts/` when present — never fetch a font at
  draw time; the repo renders offline.
- Run from the repo root with `uv run`: the uv workspace is what resolves
  `brh-core`.
- The ledger needs Postgres (`make postgres-up && make migrate`). Without it,
  only the design layer — `palette.py`, `formatting.py`, `assets.py`,
  `swatches.py` — is exercisable.
- `inventory/ledger.py` cleans titles *on read* (HTML entities, lost accents)
  and must never "fix" the source. That damage is the subject of a post.
- Charts sit on `SURFACE` (white), never on `BG` (the tinted page). The azure
  clears 3:1 on white and misses it on the tinted background.

## Scope

Keep the change minimal and say what you are *not* doing. Prefer extending an
existing pattern to inventing a parallel one. When a request needs work outside
`services/analytics` — a new query in `brh_core`, a change to the inventory
ledger, a web surface — stop and say so rather than reaching across.
